Paul Juusten
powl yoo'sten
n. (bishop of Vyborg and then of Turku, c. 1516–1575; wrote the first history of the Finnish church)
From Finnish-Swedish Juusten, a family name; Latinised Paulus Juusten.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Paul Juusten was Agricola's colleague, rival and successor. Sent like him to Wittenberg, he returned to be rector of the Turku school, became the first bishop of the new see of Vyborg in 1554, and succeeded to Turku itself in 1563. In 1569 John III sent him on an embassy to Russia, where Ivan the Terrible detained the party for three years in conditions of some cruelty; he came home broken and died two years later. His chief book is the Catalogus et ordinaria successio episcoporum Finlandensium, a catalogue of the bishops of Finland from the beginning with an account of each, which is the first Finnish church history and remains a primary source. The dictionary records him because keeping the record of faithful teachers is a duty Scripture lays on the church in plain words: “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God” (Heb 13:7).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a catalogue as a list or enumeration of names set in order; memory as the faculty of the mind by which it retains knowledge, and remembrance; and a successor as one who takes the place another has left.

expand to see more

CATALOGUE, n. [Gr.] A list or enumeration of the names of men or things disposed in a certain order, often alphabetical.

MEMORY, n. [L. memoria.] The faculty of the mind by which it retains the knowledge of previous thoughts, impressions or events; also, remembrance.

SUCCESSOR, n. One who succeeds or follows; one who takes the place which another has left, and sustains the like part or character.

CONVERSATION, n. [L. conversatio.] General course of manners; behavior; deportment, especially as it respects morals.

Key Scripture

Heb 13:7 — "Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation."

Psa 112:6 — "Surely he shall not be moved for ever: the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance."

Pro 10:7 — "The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot."

Mal 3:16 — "Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name."

Modern Corruption

Bishop of Vyborg and of Turku; three years detained by Ivan the Terrible, and author of the first history of the Finnish church.

expand to see more

The corruption to name is the Roman doctrine of apostolic succession, which converts the keeping of such a catalogue into a proof of authority: a chain of consecrations is held to guarantee the doctrine of whoever stands at the end of it. Juusten's own list disproves the claim, since it records bishops of the same see teaching contrary things. The opposite corruption is the modern indifference to a congregation's own history, which leaves each generation with no memory of who taught it and no means of noticing when the teaching changes.

The principle to recover is that the faith of former teachers is to be examined and followed where it was sound, and that God Himself keeps such a record. The psalmist promises that “the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance” (Psa 112:6). Proverbs divides the two legacies without sentiment: “The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot” (Pro 10:7). And Malachi describes the register kept in heaven, where “a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD” (Mal 3:16).

Usage

"“Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God” (Heb 13:7) — the Catalogue of the bishops of Finland."

"“The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot” (Pro 10:7) — first bishop of Vyborg, 1554."

"“a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD” (Mal 3:16) — three years detained in Russia, 1569 to 1572."
